theory.heading: What Docker for .NET is
theory.body: Docker for .NET describes the methods and patterns used within .NET Full Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Docker for .NET is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Docker for .NET matters
theory.body: Without Docker for .NET, systems built with .NET Full Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Docker for .NET works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Docker for .NET follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Docker for .NET.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Docker for .NET
theory.body: Docker for .NET offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
